checks.detail: 30,475 windows, 0 duplicate tickers, 0 duplicate close times

checks.name: Complete 15-minute schedule
checks.detail: 827 windows missing in 50 gaps (largest: 68 after 2025-12-13 05:00 UTC; 67 after 2025-12-30 08:30 UTC; 50 after 2025-12-29 08:30 UTC). Usually exchange downtime or markets Kalshi voided; rerun history.py to fill recent ones.

checks.name: Result matches settlement ≥ price to beat
checks.detail: all 27,597 checkable windows agree; 2878 windows lack a price to beat or settlement

checks.name: Chain: price to beat = previous settlement
checks.detail: 27,558 of 27,560 back-to-back pairs match exactly (99.99%); largest breaks: KXBTC15M-26MAY190530-30 (+$3), KXBTC15M-26APR241415-15 (+$0)

checks.name: Prices are sane
checks.detail: price to beat ranges $58,040–$97,730; 3 windows moved more than 3% in 15 minutes; 2878 missing or zero values

checks.name: Independent price source (Coinbase)
checks.detail: Coinbase agreed on direction in 97.8% of 90 sampled windows and 100.0% of those that finished $50+ from the line (under $25: 20/22; $25–50: 16/16; $50–100: 27/27; $100+: 25/25). Disagreement near the line is expected: Coinbase is one exchange, the index averages several. 10 windows had no candles.

checks.name: Runs test (is the sequence random?)
checks.detail: 15,746 runs vs 15,238 expected (z = +5.82, p = 0.000): more switches than chance: results tend to alternate. Check that it also holds out of sample.

checks.name: Does one result predict the next?
checks.detail: lag-1 correlation -0.0333 (z = -5.82). Statistically non-zero, but check its size: a correlation this small moves the next window's odds by only about 1.7 percentage points, less than fees cost.

checks.name: Hour-of-day lean holds out of sample?
checks.detail: Split at 2026-05-25. Hours that looked significant in the first half: 04:00; still significant, same direction, in the second half: none. Correlation of hourly leans between halves: +0.26 (near zero: the hourly pattern is noise).

checks.name: Streak behaviour holds out of sample?
checks.detail: after 3 Ups the next was Up 45.1% (first half, n=1,681) vs 48.0% (second half, n=1,732); after 3 Downs the next was Up 56.4% (first half, n=1,628) vs 52.2% (second half, n=1,815). For a fade-or-follow rule to pay, the same lean must show in both halves and be larger than the ~2–3¢ per contract that spread and fees cost.

checks.name: Kalshi price edge holds out of sample?
checks.detail: No price level was clearly profitable after fees. 7 more showed a paper profit that sits inside its error band, so it could just be luck: buy No at 70–80¢: +9.6¢ ±13.0 (n=55); buy No at 80–90¢: +6.6¢ ±9.8 (n=72); buy No at 50–60¢: +2.6¢ ±14.8 (n=48). Most windows trade under 10¢ or over 90¢; there, recent results ran -1.3¢ to +0.9¢ per contract.

checks.name: Chance findings to expect
checks.detail: The report tests 35 hour, weekday and slot groups; at 95% confidence about 1.8 would look significant by luck alone. Found: 2. That's no more than luck would produce.
